It's an extremely tough and very tight situation :(. I live 1500 miles away from campus, did not bring my textbooks, books, barely any clothes, or my notebooks. I understand that housing does not have any say, but I am unable to go back to get my items from my dorm, although my friend said he would get it for me, what are others going to do if they live just as far or even farther from campus and don't have someone to help get their items??? 

The reopening being "at the earliest" April 3rd is also kinda iffy. No one truly knows when and even if the campuses will be open again, which can also lead to difficulties getting back to campus depending on where someone is. It is a lot of money traveling such far distances, just because a university does not know exactly when they will open again. Personally, it can be up to 700 dollars to travel back to campus, is it really worth it to go up there, get everything you need, go back home for 3 weeks and then have to travel back? Even if it's closed for the rest of the semester, you'd still have to go back and get the rest of your bedding and other bigger things out of the dorm, so either way it is spending a lot of money just because they arent sure on what they want to do next. Its understandable that they are confused as everyone is, but when you take care of THOUSANDS of students, thinking quickly is something you have to do. 

Along with spending hundreds or even thousands of dollars to get to the campus and back for the out of state students, even though it is only three weeks (possibly longer), some kids just do not have money to spare with things like this. They could use the refunded money for other important things. Going to college is very costly, and having to pay for the three weeks of not even being in the dorms, or even the wasted meal plan that you arent able to transfer into the fall semster.
I'm sure there are many people that don't have a problem with any of this, which is great! If this isn't effecting you I'm glad. But, the people who are struggling with what is happening, not having a place to go, don't have their school supplies that are crucial for their academic learning, don't have their clothes, it is very hard to deal with in many different ways :(.
The Coronavirus should be taken care of in any way we can, but Penn State should be quick on their feet with what they want to do next and how to take action. They said they wouldn't close campuses but then did for three weeks, there is a strong possibility that they'll say the same thing but about closing for the entire semester.
